The line is the Aircraft Procurement, Navy 'War Consumables' line whose J-book narrative owns BRU-55 alongside its sibling suspension and release items (BRU-61, Stores Suspension and Release Equipment, Common Aircraft Armament Equipment), and the award obligates fiscal 2018 aircraft procurement (Navy) funds — a production buy of the line's own end item against the procurement line that buys it, which is the case Lens A is designed to pass. 'War Consumables' is a real armament-equipment line, not one of the catch-all titles the loader excludes, and no other PE in this index owns the BRU-55 designator, so there is no alternative owner to resolve.

refute_a.reason: Money and mission both hold: the full $20,250,603 is fiscal 2018 aircraft procurement (Navy) — BLI 0720's own account is 1506N, and the lake shows mod P00003 (2017-12-21) obligating exactly $20,250,603 under 017-1506 — the buy is Lot 5 full-rate production of the line's own BRU-55 item (the Precision Strike Weapons Program Office is only the sponsoring office, not a platform the award merely supports), and 'War Consumables' is a named armament-equipment P-1 line that does not match CATCHALL_TITLE, published once in dim_programs.

refute_b.reason: 'BRU-55' appears at exactly one pe_bli in N.tsv (0720, beside sibling BRU-61, SSRE and Common AAE); 'BRU-55A/A' is the rack's own type designation rather than a different variant or increment, the named thing is the ejector rack itself and not the contractor (EDO/Harris) or a platform, and 'Precision Strike Weapons Program Office' is a sponsoring office matching no index row — there is no rival owner to resolve.
